title: clarity is a bird I follow home
content:
from my podcast: botanical studies of internet magic
listen on spotify / listen on apple

there is a difference between wanting clarity, and wanting permission. or certainty. or safety. clarity isn't something external that I wait to happen to me (like good weather conditions), but a moving, fluid energy that I'm in conversation with -- like a bird. sometimes I see it. sometimes it's gone.

I'll explore why clarity feels so crucial for the pathless path, how people see me as having a lot of "clarity" (when in fact, I experience it as something different). I'll share what questions I ask myself for cultivating a deeper relationship to clarity.

why we want clarity

today I want to explore clarity. clarity like the holy grail of the creative path, like kind of like pulling a sword out of a stone, hoping that we have the ability and strength and integrity to do so, or like trying to walk a path that feels clear of all obstacles so that we can be sure that we won't trip over our own feet. and I think it's because especially when you're doing something different on the edge of what reality is for most people, we can feel swirly, cloudy, stormy, desert-y inside. we want someone else to tell us what to do. give me a plan, help me be clear with myself.

to begin this exploration, I would ask you, where in your life do you long for more clarity? do you want clarity? or do you want permission to do the thing?

when I'm thinking about a minimalist, non-exhaustive list of what we want, what I want as creative people making their way in the world, I would boil it down to three things. one, creative expression and fulfillment that is making the work that really matters to me in a way that feels satisfying. like this is why I'm on earth. two, money, energetic reciprocity, sustainability, abundance, a channel, an infinity mirror way of supporting ourselves with our creative energy without compromising our values or needing to compartmentalize ourselves in a way that feels depleting. and three, which is the focus of this episode, clarity. knowing that we're on the right path to the right destination, to creative expression and money, and sustainability, which clarity describes, this is the right path, this is the how, this is the what, this is what I will do next. and yes, I can make this work. and yes, I know who I am.

this feels like a lot to need clarity for.

clarity as good weather

and I think sometimes we think of clarity as like the weather, something that happens to us, having good weather and having a map. the fantasy is that there are clear skies, we have permission to launch the ship, or sail the boat, we have an unobstructed path, and we know where we're going. and the fear is that the weather will be bad. there will be fog and storms and murky waters and swamps, and we will either run into disaster or we will be paralyzed.

sometimes clarity comes in what you don't want. like I know I'm clear that I don't want to be on social media, or I'm clear that there's a type of client that I want to work with and don't want to work with. and sometimes that clarity is about having boundaries, boundaries as a container that can condense energy and keep you safe, help you focus your energy so that it's not leaking everywhere. sometimes clarity is about being able to have foresight, have visibility to see into the future like a seer or like someone with great vision to know what will happen next.

as I'm speaking this, I'm thinking about the high priestess, the card in the tarot where the clarity that the high priestess has is internal, it's a deep inner knowing, not about external visibility, but internal vision.

conviction over clarity

oftentimes I notice that people come to my world and write me and tell me they admire me for having what it seems like a lot of clarity. but my confession is that what comes off as clarity on the outside, sometimes that perception surprises me because I don't necessarily experience it like that. what I experience is not clear skies, I experience tsunami weather all the time.

what they see as clarity, I experience as commitment and conviction. like I am committed to doing this thing even when I don't know if it'll work, if it will totally fail, if I will fall on my face and I feel conviction in what I believe is true for me. I don't dare to suppose this is true for everyone, but I know how I feel. and I know how I want to exist in the world and I want to be unapologetically in integrity with myself and my choices. and this is often interpreted as extreme stubbornness. like I will go off into the wild on my own adventure because I know this is what I have to do even if I look like a total fool.

is that clarity? or is it just being uncompromisingly me?

and I can't tell you how many times I've had friends or peers ask me very gently, but are you sure you want to say no to this thing, to this client or to being on social media or can't you find a different way of doing this? and I'm an Aries moon, so it always would trigger this burst of explosive anger that may or may not be revealed. and I'd be like, no, I don't want to do that. and of course there's a tiny voice in my head that says, but maybe they're right. maybe I should be more pliable. maybe the middle road is better for me. and yet I never did it. I never did the thing. and as a result, many years later, it seems to others that I have clarity.

so what I mean is clarity is experienced not as a constant state, not as a thing that I've conquered. it's the result of a capacity to be committed to what is true inside of me. it's not about external certainty. it's about internal conviction.

expecting a long road

for many, many years while I was doing my stubborn thing, I would wake up with so much amnesia on some days and wondering if what I'm doing makes any sense to anyone. those were the days when I had a website practice and I had a daily practice of writing or drawing something in 30 minutes, hitting publish and letting it go. and there was no strategy, no plan, no idea as to how this would make me money or build an audience. it was none of that. it was just about daily release.

in those days, no one came to my website. I barely sent a newsletter maybe once a year. I didn't have a podcast or an audience. I barely taught courses. I made most of my money through web design clients who never read my work. and so I didn't see how all of this would make sense, but I kept doing it because I felt clear in myself that I had to.

and in my experience, those external signals of, yes, you're on the right path. yes, this is working, of recognition or validation, they do come very, very slowly over a period of time, maybe part of having clarity is stretching your capacity for endurance for the long road.

I think social media has primed our brains to expect immediate validation, the dopamine hit of, if I jump, will they catch me with a like or with a share or with a comment? whereas clarity comes through the action of the jump again and again. you cannot wait for validation to come to give you that clarity. you yourself must give yourself permission and then the clarity will arrive.

clarity is not the same as permission. it's not a promise of certainty. it's not a guarantee. it's not a paved path that's ready and cushy for you to land on. it's the energy that inspires the moment of the leap forwards.

clarity as a bird I follow

and so you can take a next step forward before you know where you're going to land or you can know and you cannot know. sometimes I feel clarity and I take action on that clarity and then the outcome or the result leads me somewhere completely different. and there's beauty in that too because ultimately it's not about having a perfectly accurate map of external reality. clarity is about seeing internally, knowing what feels right for you in this next moment.

so instead of wanting the reassurance of clear skies, perhaps we can think of clarity as an energy, as a momentum, as a directional force that happens and can happen in any weather condition, which is why the last couple of days it came to me that perhaps clarity as a metaphor could be a bird that I follow that is not something, not a landscape that is fixed, that has certainty and safety, but a living thing that is in motion with its own life cycles.

a bird is not something that I want to cage as my pet. I'm not against having birds as pets by the way, but personally I think I would feel a little bit sad to see a bird in a cage and clarity as a bird is not something that I want to keep caged as my pet or try to extract from or help me feel secure. I want to walk on the path and keep my palm open so that clarity can land there. I want to listen to its bird song through the trees and sense where it is, even if it sometimes feels very distant and just like a faint sound in the forest.

if clarity is a bird, then it's a being that I can be in conversation with. I'm feeling this thing. I see you, I will follow you, even when I'm scared, even when it's dark, even when I don't know where this road is leading exactly.

the practice of seeking clarity

clarity comes through asking questions. it's through the practice of questioning and being with the questions. and so clarity itself comes through a result of practice and process like everything else.

the questions I like to ask myself when I'm journaling, when I'm walking, just holding it in the back of my mind is what do I need right now? what would feel nourishing to me? where's my energy and inspiration naturally going? what is totally irrelevant and just mind noise? what feels urgent, even though it's not urgent? what feels true? and what can I experiment with?

I want to remind you again that clarity exists only in the present moment, but life is a string of present moments. it doesn't end until we die. and so the more you listen to the clarity, the more that it can be a dance between what you know and what you don't know, what you ask and how you respond.

and maybe after some weeks or months or years or decades of listening and speaking with this bird and following the path that it's led you down, maybe you'll turn around and see that the path you've carved is very clear. it appears very clear maybe by that point in the different seasons of your life. clarity will not feel like something elusive that exists outside of you, that is good weather conditions granted by the gods, but instead a living thing, a bird, a being, a spirit that's always been inside of you all along.

clarity is not something you have or don't have. it's something that you're in relationship with all the time.
